from_notes: FBR fuel MOX (Pu-239 + U-238); FBTR plutonium-uranium mixed carbide
from_notes_src: PMF S&T Part 4 p.45-46 (FBR, FBTR carbide fuel); Rocket CA 2026 Part 01 p.162 (PFBR criticality; fuel not stated)
x: The Kalpakkam fast breeders run on plutonium: FBTR on plutonium-uranium mixed carbide, PFBR on MOX (Pu-239 + U-238). Uranium-238 is only the fertile blanket; thorium is a Stage III fuel.
source: PMF S&T Part 4 p.45-46 (FBR, FBTR carbide fuel); Rocket CA 2026 Part 01 p.162 (PFBR criticality; fuel not stated)

x: Apsara went critical in 1956, CIRUS in 1960, Zerlina in 1961 and KAMINI in 1996, so the order is C, A, B, D. CIRUS (with Canada) came before the zero-energy Zerlina.
source: PMF S&T Part 5 p.8-9 (BARC research reactors); https://www.barc.gov.in (research reactors: Apsara 1956, CIRUS 1960, Zerlina 1961); IGCAR (KAMINI 1996)
evidence: BARC research reactor history (Zerlina critical 14 Jan 1961)

from_notes: Apsara: critical 1956; India's and Asia's first research reactor
from_notes_src: PMF S&T Part 5 p.8-9 (Apsara 1956, first reactor)
x: Apsara (BARC, Trombay, critical 4 August 1956) was India's and Asia's first research reactor. CIRUS came in 1960, Dhruva in 1985 and KAMINI in 1996.
source: PMF S&T Part 5 p.8-9 (Apsara 1956, first reactor)

x: The Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (est. 1971) is at Kalpakkam, Tamil Nadu. Trombay houses BARC; Indore has RRCAT.
source: PMF S&T Part 5 p.12 (IGCAR, Kalpakkam)

from_notes_src: PMF S&T Part 5 p.8-9 (Apsara built indigenously)
x: Apsara (1956) was designed and built by Indian scientists at Trombay, making it the first reactor built with Indian effort. KAMINI (1996) and Purnima came later; Rohini is a satellite/rocket series.
source: PMF S&T Part 5 p.8-9 (Apsara built indigenously)

from_notes: CIRUS, Dhruva, Purnima: research reactors at Trombay
from_notes_src: PMF S&T Part 5 p.8-9 (BARC research reactors)
x: Dhruva, Purnima and CIRUS are all research reactors at BARC, Trombay. None of them is a star, a book or a power plant.
source: PMF S&T Part 5 p.8-9 (BARC research reactors)

x: Tummalapalle uranium project (UCIL) is in YSR Kadapa district, so A is correct. KPM (Kylleng-Pyndengsohiong-Mawthabah, Domiasiat) is in West Khasi Hills, Meghalaya, not Guntur; AP's Guntur/Palnadu deposit is Koppunuru, so B is wrong.
source: PMF Lens Sep 2026 p.7 (Tummalapalle AP; Domiasiat Meghalaya); Lok Sabha reply (eparlib.nic.in AU1559: Tummalapalle YSR, Koppunuru Palnadu); UCIL (KPM, West Khasi Hills)
evidence: PMF Human & Economic Geography Part 4 EG-MR-110 (Tummalapalle)

x: 'Atomic energy and mineral resources necessary for its production' is Entry 6 of the Union List (List I, Seventh Schedule), so only Parliament legislates on it.
source: Laxmikanth Indian Polity, Seventh Schedule List I Entry 6

x: Pitchblende (uraninite, UO2/U3O8) is the chief ore of uranium. Monazite, not pitchblende, is the thorium ore.
source: PMF Human & Economic Geography Part 4 EG-MR-110 (uranium ores); NCERT Class X Geography ch.5

x: The DAE's Atomic Minerals Directorate established the Tummalapalle uranium deposit in YSR Kadapa district; UCIL mines and processes it there. Kamahalapalli, Pagidipalli and Nagulapalli are not uranium sites.
source: PMF Lens Sep 2026 p.7 (Tummalapalle in AP); PMF Human & Economic Geography Part 4 EG-MR-110

from_notes: Monazite = principal thorium ore; beach sands of Kerala
from_notes_src: PMF S&T Part 5 p.1-4 (monazite = thorium ore)
x: Kerala's coastal beach sands hold monazite, the principal ore of thorium. Uranium, chromite and graphite are not the monazite mineral.
source: PMF S&T Part 5 p.1-4 (monazite = thorium ore)

from_notes: Monazite: thorium + rare earths; not the entire coast; only IREL may process and export it
from_notes_src: PMF S&T Part 5 p.1-4 (monazite, IREL); PMF Human & Economic Geography Part 4 (monazite)
x: Monazite is a source of rare earths and contains thorium (1, 2 correct). It occurs only in some coastal stretches (Kerala, TN, Odisha, AP), not the entire coast (3 wrong), and only the government body IREL may process or export it (4 correct) – so 1, 2 and 4.
source: PMF S&T Part 5 p.1-4 (monazite, IREL); PMF Human & Economic Geography Part 4 (monazite)

from_notes_src: PMF S&T Part 5 p.1-4 (monazite = thorium ore)
x: Monazite is the principal ore of thorium (with rare earths such as lanthanum and cerium). Zirconium comes from zircon, titanium from ilmenite/rutile.
source: PMF S&T Part 5 p.1-4 (monazite = thorium ore)

x: Pitchblende is the main uranium ore, and uranium is the fuel of nuclear power stations. Bauxite (aluminium), quartz and feldspar are not nuclear fuels.
source: PMF S&T Part 4 p.24, 38 (uranium fuel); PMF Human & Economic Geography Part 4 EG-MR-110

from_notes_src: PMF S&T Part 5 p.1-4 (monazite thorium, Kerala sands)
x: The monazite beach sands of Kerala are rich in thorium, which causes the high natural radioactivity along the coast. Plutonium is not natural there; zinc is not radioactive.
source: PMF S&T Part 5 p.1-4 (monazite thorium, Kerala sands)

x: ITER is the world's largest magnetic-confinement plasma experiment (B) and India is a member (D). A is wrong – it is a fusion, not fission, tokamak; C is wrong – the host EU pays about 45%, the US about 9%.
source: PMF S&T Part 4 p.27, 50 (ITER tokamak, members); https://www.iter.org (cost sharing: Europe ~45%, others ~9% each)

x: I is true (ITER aims to show fusion's feasibility), II is true (ITER-India, the domestic agency, sits at IPR Gandhinagar) and IV lists the seven members. III is false: Aditya, IPR's medium-size tokamak, was commissioned in 1989, long before ITER, and is not part of ITER (printed key: all four).
source: PMF S&T Part 4 p.27, 50 (ITER, members); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ADITYA_(tokamak) (citing IPR: built 1982-89); https://www.iter.org (ITER-India at IPR)
evidence: ipr.res.in / Wikipedia ADITYA (tokamak): commissioned 1989, IPR's own machine
iter.org: ITER Agreement signed 2006; ITER-India domestic agency at IPR

from_notes: Members EU + India, China, Japan, South Korea, Russia, USA – Canada is not a member
x: The ITER Agreement (2006) was signed by the EU, India, China, Japan, South Korea, Russia and the USA; Canada left the project in 2003 and is not a member.
source: PMF S&T Part 4 p.27, 50 (ITER members)

from_notes_src: PMF S&T Part 4 p.50 (ITER, Cadarache, France)

source: PMF S&T Part 4 p.50 (ITER, Cadarache, France)

from_notes: Fusion reactors work on fusion of light nuclei in a tokamak; ITER = fusion experiment
from_notes_src: PMF S&T Part 4 p.27, 50 (fusion reactors, ITER)
x: ITER is an experimental fusion reactor, so its success would let India build fusion reactors for power. Thorium use concerns fission breeders, fission efficiency is unrelated, and satellite navigation has nothing to do with ITER.
source: PMF S&T Part 4 p.27, 50 (fusion reactors, ITER)

from_notes: December 2022: fusion ignition at NIF, Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory
from_notes_src: PMF S&T Part 4 p.29 (NIF, LLNL, Dec 2022)
x: In December 2022 the National Ignition Facility at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory achieved fusion ignition with net energy gain using lasers. Los Alamos and Oak Ridge were not involved, so 'more than one' is wrong.
source: PMF S&T Part 4 p.29 (NIF, LLNL, Dec 2022)

from_notes: DAE: set up 1954; under the PM
from_notes_src: PMF S&T Part 5 p.4-12 (DAE under the PM)
x: The Department of Atomic Energy (1954) works directly under the Prime Minister, who holds the DAE portfolio. It is not part of the Ministry of Power or the Ministry of Science and Technology.
source: PMF S&T Part 5 p.4-12 (DAE under the PM)
